doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His father's work as a lumber inspector for General Motors
summary: Elvin explains his father picked the lumber used in car and bus frames, and when the family left Vicksburg.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: He was a lumber inspector for general motors.
Could you describe what he did?

(Laughs) Well in the 20’s and the early 30’s most of the cars and busses and all that, they had wooden framework on the inside of the car. They had upholstery attached to that, and the steel would go over the top. So that was how cars were made .They used a lot of lumber and my Dad he was the one that would select the lumber to go into the cars and the busses. That was his job.
Do you have any idea when they left Vicksburg, Mississippi and came to Pontiac?
That was um… I know it was um…I guess it was just after World War I, 1918 or something.
